- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% of forecast value for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use a 7-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
